thread:
customer-jane: Hey team — noticed my trial credits didn’t drop after a bunch of successful streaming generations this morning. Account: acct_7Gk5, using the JS SDK with websocket streams. Billing page shows 0 delta. Any ideas?

sara-support: Sorry about that — can you confirm if you were using the streaming endpoint (ws / sse) and whether you closed the connection early? Also send one example request_id if you have it.

customer-jane: Yep streaming via websockets. Example request_id: req_20260317_4312. I didn’t intentionally close early, but the UI sometimes cancels when I switch tabs. Using SDK v1.3.0.

sara-support: Thanks. Looping in eng runtime and billing for ledger + trace: @tom-eng @liam-billing :eyes:

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0317-78 (assigned to eng-runtime)

tom-eng: Hi @customer-jane — could you paste the minimal snippet used to open the stream? Also, if you have raw websocket logs (open/close frames) that helps. I’ll check request traces for req_20260317_4312.

customer-jane: minimal snippet: ```js const ws = new WebSocket('wss://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-chat'); ws.send(JSON.stringify({prompt: 'summarize...', stream: true})); // receiving chunks then I do ws.close() when done ``` I don't have full raw frames, only client logs showing ws.close at 10:23:41.

liam-billing: I queried the billing ledger for acct_7Gk5 and req_20260317_4312. No billing event recorded for that session — looks like the billing pipeline didn't get a final "stream_end" event. Opening billing trace with trace_id trace_BX-88, forward to eng.

tom-eng: Found the trace. The streaming session connected and emitted token deltas as partial events, but the final end event never arrived to the stream-collector service because an older SDK (<=1.3.0) sends a TCP FIN without the proper end-of-stream JSON envelope when the client calls ws.close() during mid-chunk. Our collector treats that as an aborted session and doesn't emit a billing event.

sara-support: Is this a known bug? Is there a mitigation for existing users who lost credits? :confused:

tom-eng: We saw a small set of customers hit this pattern. Root cause: SDK websocket close behavior + stream-collector's conservative billing rule. Fix options: 1) short term — billing can retroactively reconcile sessions that had partial deltas but no end marker by joining traces and attributing token deltas; 2) medium term — update stream-collector to accept TCP-close with partial buffer flush; 3) recommend customers upgrade SDK.

liam-billing: We can run a reconciliation job for affected accounts. If you want immediate credits, we can apply manual adjustments and a protection credit while we run the job. Tom — estimate for collector patch?

tom-eng: Collector patch will be ready as PR today and can be rolled to canary within 24 hours. Full rollout in ~48 hours after smoke tests. Reconciliation job will run once patch is live to pick up any sessions that previously lacked end markers; should complete within 6 hours for the affected time window.

sara-support: @customer-jane we can apply a provisional credit equal to the estimated token usage for the session(s) you listed while we reconcile. Do you want that now?

customer-jane: Yes please, that’d be great. Appreciate the fast help.

liam-billing: Done — provisional credit applied: +500 trial tokens (visible in the UI). We’ll mark the account for the reconciliation run and follow up when it's complete. INC-2026-0317-78 updated.

customer-jane: Thank you! I’ll upgrade SDK to 1.4.2 and monitor.

oncall-bot: INC-2026-0317-78 status: triaged -> in_progress (eng-runtime)

tom-eng: Patch note: SDK v1.4.2 changes close behavior to send final "stream_end" envelope before socket close; recommend upgrade. We'll keep you posted after the reconciliation job finishes.

customer-jane: Sounds good — will report back if anything else crops up. :thumbsup:
